newsitem.title: KUWAIT: UAE, U.S. to discuss issues blocking F-16 deal.
newsitem.headline: UAE, U.S. to discuss issues blocking F-16 deal.

text.p: The United States said on Monday the United Arab Emirates was not linking its demand to amend a defence pact with its planned purchase of up to 80 long-range warplanes worth some $6 billion.
"There is no linkage," U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen told a news conference in Kuwait before leaving for Bahrain to continue his Gulf tour which will also include the UAE and Oman.

But a Gulf Arab official source said that Abu Dhabi was "indirectly" linking its request to amend the 1994 defence pact with Washington to the purchase and was also keen to see a breakthrough in the Middle East peace process.

Lockheed Martin Corp F-16s are high on the list for the UAE requirement and one Gulf defence source said that Saudi Arabia's talks on the purchase of up to 100 of the aircraft "have advanced in recent weeks".

"The UAE cannot appear to be rewarding the U.S. with a plane deal at a time when Israel is seen by Arab states blocking the peace talks," said a Gulf Arab analyst. "They want to see the Americans moving the process forward."

The UAE's main arms procurement officer, armed forces chief of staff Sheikh Mohammad bin Zayed al-Nahayan, late last month held a low-profile meeting in Geneva with U.S. Deputy Defence Secretary John White to discuss Abu Dhabi's demands to amend a 1994 defence pact and the possible purchase of U.S. warplanes.

"This matter has been under discussion for some time," Cohen said. "I don't believe there is any significant change as of this time...I believe the negotiations concerning the security of forces and stationing of forces is still under negotiation."
U.S. naval forces patrolling the Gulf often visit the UAE and defence sources say as many as 400,000 American military personnel stop in the UAE every year.

The UAE wants to amend the defence pact, granting it jurisdiction if a U.S. military personnel commits an offence while on shore leave. Defence sources say the UAE enjoys that right under similar pacts with Britain and France.

Cohen did not say if Washington was willing to amend the pact but Gulf Arab defence sources said Abu Dhabi could settle for a modified version of one of the U.S. options on offer to tackle the jurisdiction issue.
"Things are better than before," said a source familiar with the talks. "I think the UAE is more optimistic than before and a solution could be on the way."

The F-16 is in a fierce race with France's Dassault Aviation to win the Abu Dhabi deal. Also competing is the Eurofighter 2000, made by a consortium of British Aerospace, Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA), Spain's CASA and Italy's Alenia Spa.
In recent weeks Abu Dhabi officials have also held low-key meetings with Britain and France to discuss the deal.

"The competition is very fierce and they (manufacturers) are desperate to win the contract," said a Gulf source familiar with the talks. "The offers have been changed again and they are giving very interesting options."
